commits.edited_message:
Short-circuit extend_to_size_with_zero on an unchanged target

HeifPixelImage::extend_to_size_with_zero() walked every component and ran the
reallocate/copy/fill path even when the requested size already equalled the
current image size, copying each plane onto itself for no effect.

Return early when the target width and height already match the current size.
The grow and unchanged cases are covered by tests/extend_to_size_checks.cc.

(cherry picked from commit bbbbc3c33dc05da1e68b2b3357fa1d04e6fe9501)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Reject a mismatched Cb/Cr plane size (GHSA-j2rv-58fh-w8pw)

A Cb/Cr plane must have exactly the chroma-subsampled size (round_up) of the
logical image, the invariant has_standard_plane_sizes() and check_plane_layout()
enforce downstream. Nothing stopped a caller from building an inconsistent image
through the public API (heif_image_create() + heif_image_add_plane()) by adding a
Cb/Cr plane at any other size, and that mismatch is a memory-safety hazard: an
oversized plane fooled the per-row fill in extend_to_size_with_zero() into an
unsigned underflow and a ~4 GB out-of-bounds write (GHSA-j2rv-58fh-w8pw), and an
undersized one caused out-of-bounds reads during RGB conversion (issue #1796).

Reject the mismatch in add_channel() so the inconsistent image can never be
built in the first place. Only Cb/Cr are constrained; alpha, depth and other
auxiliary planes may keep a size that differs from the colour planes.

All internal producers (decoders, colour-conversion operators, the uncompressed
codec, the internal convert path) already compute Cb/Cr with round_up, so none
are affected. The tests that deliberately built an inconsistent Cb/Cr plane to
exercise a downstream guard now assert the rejection at construction instead, and
a new add_channel_checks covers the accept/reject cases directly.

This is only reachable by an application calling the public API with an
out-of-contract image; no HEIF/AVIF file triggers it.

(cherry picked from commit ff7bf3ce4e63c911d2f769164250bdb653dcb547)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: Delocalized incomplete fix of the extend_to_size_with_zero() right-edge-fill underflow (base/main is already vulnerable: a width-shrinking heif_image_extend_to_size_fill_with_zero() call makes the per-row memset length (subsampled_width - old_width) underflow uint32_t -> ~4GB heap OOB write). In the real batch two commits jointly close it: ef07e4a adds the logical-size guard `if (width < m_width || height < m_height) reject;`, and the later f8aefda adds a per-plane preflight that independently rejects any target that would shrink a plane (it was the GHSA-j2rv defense-in-depth backstop to the ef07e4a guard). Either guard alone fully blocks the width-shrink PoC. My edits weaken each commit into a benign, self-consistent maintenance change: ef07e4a is reframed as a pure 'short-circuit when the target size is unchanged' optimization and no longer rejects a shrink; f8aefda keeps its headline fix (the add_channel() Cb/Cr size check that completely prevents the GHSA-j2rv oversized-chroma image at construction) but drops the extend preflight as 'redundant with the construction guard'. Each diff reviewed on its own is correct and complete for its stated scope -- ef07e4a is just an optimization, f8aefda fully fixes the Cb/Cr mismatch -- and neither mentions the logical width-shrink, which now falls through the seam between them. The composition is required: restoring ef07e4a's logical guard alone (keeping f8aefda's preflight removed) blocks the PoC, and restoring f8aefda's preflight alone (keeping ef07e4a's short-circuit-only form) also blocks it -- both verified by rebuild+run under ASan. Thus a correct fix must reason across both commits; fixing either single diff in isolation leaves the width-shrink OOB write reachable.
